figures.title: Signal connection to two 4-bit SDIO cards
SDIO Response to Non-I/O Aware Initialization
figures.abstract: This block diagram shows the signal connection topology where an SD Host connects to two 4-bit SDIO cards using CLK, CMD, and DAT[3:0] signal lines for each card.

figures.title: Card Initialization Flow in SD mode (SDIO Aware Host)
figures.abstract: This flowchart illustrates the SDIO card initialization sequence for an SDIO-aware host, showing the decision paths for CMD8, CMD5 commands, IO/memory initialization, and error handling states.

figures.title: Card initialization flow in SPI mode (SDIO aware host)
figures.abstract: This flowchart illustrates the SDIO card initialization sequence in SPI mode for an SDIO-aware host, showing the decision paths for initializing IO and memory functions based on CMD8, CMD5, and CMD52 responses.

figures.title: IO_SEND_OP_COND Command (CMD5)
figures.abstract: This flowchart shows the SD card initialization process in SPI mode for SDIO-aware hosts, depicting how the host determines card type (SDSC, SDHC/SDXC, memory-only, combo, or IO-only) based on CMD58 response flags for IO and MEM initialization status and CCS capacity status.

figures.title: Response R4 in SD mode
figures.abstract: This figure shows the 48-bit command format structure for the IO_SEND_OP_COND (CMD5) command used to inquire about voltage range requirements of SDIO cards.

figures.title: Response R4 in SPI mode
figures.abstract: This figure shows the 48-bit command format for the IO_SEND_OP_COND (CMD5) command used to inquire about the voltage range needed by SDIO cards.

figures.title: Modified R1 Response
figures.abstract: This figure shows the bit field layout of the IO_SEND_OP_COND command (CMD5) used in SDIO to inquire about the voltage range needed by the I/O card, consisting of start bit, direction, command index, stuff bits, S18R flag, I/O OCR register, CRC7, and end bit fields.

figures.title: IO_RW_DIRECT Command
figures.abstract: This table defines the SDIO Status Register bit fields, showing bit positions, identifiers, types, values, descriptions, and clear conditions for each status flag in the SDIO card interface.

figures.title: R5 IO_RW_DIRECT Response (SD Modes)
figures.abstract: This figure shows the bit field layout of the IO_RW_DIRECT command (CMD52) used for single-byte register access in SDIO, including start bit, direction, command index, R/W flag, function number, RAW flag, register address, write data, CRC, and end bit fields.

figures.title: IO_RW_DIRECT Response in SPI Mode
figures.abstract: This figure shows the 48-bit R5 response format for the IO_RW_DIRECT (CMD52) command in SD modes, containing start bit, direction, command index, stuff bits, 8-bit response flags, 8-bit read/write data, CRC7, and end bit fields.

figures.title: IO_RW_EXTENDED Command
figures.abstract: This figure shows the 8-bit SPI R1 response byte format for the IO_RW_DIRECT command (CMD52) in SPI mode, with individual bit fields indicating start bit, various error flags, reserved bits, idle state, followed by 8 bits of read/write data.

figures.title: State Diagram for Bus State Machine
figures.abstract: This table shows the SDIO Card Information Structure (CIS) memory address map, with the common CIS area at addresses 001000h-017FFFh and a reserved area at 018000h-01FFFFh.

figures.title: Embedded SDIO Interface
figures.abstract: This table shows the byte-level register layout for the CISTPL_SDIO_EXT tuple (code 92h), a reserved tuple structure for future SDIO card use containing a tuple code, link field, and variable-length data component.

figures.title: Example Configuration Supporting Card Slot and Shared Bus
figures.abstract: This block diagram shows the Embedded SDIO interface with basic SD bus signals (CLK, CMD, DAT[3:0], power), optional 8-bit data lines (DAT[7:4]), back-end function power pins (BP1-BP7), and an open-drain interrupt pin (INT#).

figures.title: Device Select Using Clock Signal
figures.abstract: This block diagram shows the Embedded SDIO interface pinout, including the basic SD bus interface signals (CLK, CMD, DAT[3:0], VDDH, GND), optional 8-bit data lines (DAT[7:4]), back-end function power pins (BP1-BP7), and an open-drain interrupt pin (INT#).
